conventions.expectations: Every expectation is written by hand from the profile contract and the profile spec. None is recorded from a host run.
conventions.worker: Each run starts a new worker process: <host> extension worker --abi <declaredAbi> --module <wasm> --build-identity <identity> --json, with --request-bytes, --response-bytes and --instructions when the case's worker object gives requestBytes, responseBytes or instructions. <identity> is result.buildIdentity of the morphir/command-result that <host> extension worker --help --json writes, read once for the host. worker.omit names arguments the runs leave out. worker.buildIdentity other passes the host's identity with its last hexadecimal digit changed.
conventions.identity: The runner is given the host's offering, platform and engine, because a worker reports none of them. A report without them is refused.
conventions.profiles: The runner is given the profiles the host declares to run. A case applies to a host that declares its appliesTo profile and is recorded as not_applicable for any other. extism-kernel-v1 is the required profile, so its cases apply to every host.
conventions.frames: A run writes its frames in order, each as a Content-Length framed message whose body is the UTF-8 of the frame's value serialized compactly with members in the order written. After the last frame, stdin stays open until the worker exits.
conventions.exitCode: The worker's exit status: 0 served until its instance ended; 1 a fault, an invalid frame, or stdin ended first; 2 bad arguments; 3 a refusal before any request. Absent means not constrained.
conventions.stdout: stdoutBytes is the byte count of all of stdout. stdoutFrames lists every frame on stdout, in order. Two JSON values are equal when they have the same type and value: object members in any order, array elements in order, numbers by numeric value and strings by code point. A frame matches when its body parses to a JSON value equal to json, or equal to the body of the run's frame sameAsFrame, or satisfying every pointers entry (an RFC 6901 pointer with equals, a JSON value, or type, a JSON type name).
conventions.events: events lists stderr events that must appear in this order, possibly among others. A matcher names the event and may fix abi (started), code and messageIncludes (refused; each string must occur in error.message) or kind (fault; absent means any kind). noEvents names events that must not appear. Every started event's moduleSha256 must equal the module's sha256. Every started event's bounds must have exactly the members memoryCeiling, instructionBudget and callDeadline, each {"enforced": true} or {"enforced": false, "reason": r} with r one of the contract's reasons. Every fault event's fault must have kind and may have message, and nothing else.
conventions.guestOutput: guestOutput lists strings that must occur, in order, in the text of the run's output events joined in their order with nothing between them. guestOutputIncludes lists strings that must each occur in that text, in any order. noGuestOutput lists strings that must not occur in it.
conventions.timing: withinSeconds.range is measured from the end of the write of the run's last frame to the first fault event (until: fault) or to the worker's exit (until: exit).
conventions.alternatives: A run with alternatives passes when the observation satisfies one alternative whose when matches: {bound, enforced} matches what the started event's bounds declare for that bound; {hostRuns, runs} matches whether the host declares the profile hostRuns. Two alternatives may have the same when; the host may then show either. A run that expects budget-exhausted under the default budget also has a call-deadline alternative for the same when, because the budget unit is engine-defined and the deadline may come first.
conventions.bounds: A case's bounds are the bounds it exercises. When the host declares one of them not enforced, the case is recorded as not_enforced, not as passed or failed.
conventions.gaps: A case's gaps say what the contract leaves open about the observation; the expectation stops there.
conventions.withoutCase: withoutCase lists the contract elements that no case covers, each with the reason. Every other contract element has at least one case.

Not observable through a worker: the worker reports the fault kind, and the host session that reads the report gives the code.
Not observable through a worker: the worker reports the fault kind, and the host session that reads the report gives the outcome.
Not observable through a worker: the worker reports the fault kind, and the host session that reads the report gives the code.
Not observable through a worker: the host session refuses the frame before any worker reads it. limits/request-over-limit covers the worker's own frame check.
Not observable through a worker: the worker applies --response-bytes before the host session sees the frame. limits/response-over-limit covers the worker's own check.
Not observable through a worker: the worker does not check the JSON-RPC version or ids, and the runner reads its frames directly.
Not observable through a worker: the profiles a host runs are in its runtime report, which the runner takes as an input.
Not observable through a worker: cancellation is a host-session outcome, and the contract does not say what an interrupted worker does.
No case covers it: every module of the corpus is assembled from text, so the corpus has no file that is unreadable or not a well-formed WASM module.
No case needs it: the runner reads the build identity from --help --json before any run, so a worker without it cannot be qualified at all.

gaps: The contract does not say how a runner observes that the module was not instantiated; exit status 3 with no started event is the observable part.

gaps: Of the worker defaults, this case observes the --call-ms default of 30000. The --memory-pages default shows in the memory cases. The --request-bytes, --response-bytes and --instructions defaults are not observed: they would need a frame over 6 MiB, a response over 16 MiB, or a guest whose instruction count is known under every engine.
The budget unit is engine-defined, so a metering host may reach the call deadline before it uses the default budget. Either bound may end the call. bounds/small-budget tests exhaustion on its own.

gaps: The fault kind is not constrained. A host that observes refused growth reports memory-limit, another host trap, and started.bounds does not say which kind of host it is.
The contract does not fix the order of the method and the URL in the output event. That no connection is made is not observable here.
poll_oneoff asks for a 10-second timeout. Errno 76 returns at once; the range only bounds a host that blocks or stops the guest instead.
That the root is a private, empty directory is not observable from the guest without WASI file access, which the sandbox denies; only its type is checked.
The guest calls morphir_log at the level trace, so its marker shows that morphir_log is not filtered.
